albums.blurb: Mort Garson was a Juilliard-trained Canadian arranger who spent the 1950s writing pop charts before becoming one of the first composers to build entire records on the Moog synthesizer. Plantasia, subtitled “warm earth music for plants and the people who love them,” was composed entirely on the Moog and never properly sold: it was given away with houseplant purchases from the Mother Earth boutique on Melrose Avenue in Los Angeles and with Simmons mattresses from Sears. It sat in obscurity until online rediscovery led Sacred Bones to reissue it in 2019, complete with plantable wildflower-seed packaging.
albums.reception: Essentially unheard on release, it became a posthumous cult hit decades later, and Pitchfork rated the 2019 Sacred Bones reissue 7.2, calling it perhaps Garson's most beloved album among crate-diggers and record collectors.

albums.blurb: Kendrick Lamar's third studio album and the follow-up to good kid, m.A.A.d city trades that record's cinematic gangsta-rap narrative for a dense fusion of funk, jazz, and soul, built with a live-musician core that includes Thundercat, Terrace Martin, Robert Glasper, and Kamasi Washington, plus production from Flying Lotus and a George Clinton appearance. Released on Interscope in March 2015, it sits at the center of the decade's jazz-and-hip-hop crossover and seeded the follow-up compilation untitled unmastered.
albums.reception: The album debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 and won the Grammy Award for Best Rap Album in 2016, when Lamar received eleven nominations in a single year.

albums.blurb: Beach House is the Baltimore duo of singer-organist Victoria Legrand and guitarist Alex Scally, and Teen Dream is their third album and Sub Pop debut, recorded in a converted church studio in upstate New York. It marked the leap from the hazy, drum-machine miniatures of their first two records to full-bodied arrangements, and it became the duo's breakout, setting the template for the dream pop revival that ran through the 2010s.
albums.reception: Pitchfork designated it Best New Music, publications including Rolling Stone, NME, Spin, and Paste placed it on their best-albums-of-2010 lists, and Pitchfork later ranked it No. 21 among the best albums of the 2010s.
